source.check: returned unopposed: selected as the Unionist candidate for the division (Impartial Reporter, 8 May 1958, p. 7); the Reporter of 22 May 1958 (p. 7) states that 'all the members were returned unopposed for the County Council and the three Rural Councils'; sat as a member of the new council (Impartial Reporter, 12 June 1958, p. 7)

note: Triennial election of Enniskillen Rural District Council, polled Thursday 5 June 1958. No contests. The Impartial Reporter of 22 May 1958, p. 7, records that no nominations were received for three seats previously held by Nationalists — Tempo (Mr. Arthur Fee), Ballyreagh (Mr. Jas. Owens) and Kinawley, vacant for the last term and formerly represented by Mr. P. T. O'Reilly — that Mr. Joseph Smyth succeeds Mr. Edmund J. Joy in Doagh, and that Mr. Hugh Corrigan replaces the late Mr. James Murphy in Drumane. The same paper of 15 May 1958, p. 5, prints Mr. John Wilson as returned for Drummee, in place of Mr. Frederick Montgomery. Other members are recorded where a selection list or a report of the new council's meetings names them, each division inferred from the 1955 return (Fermanagh Herald, 4 June 1955, p. 8). Filled from the Impartial Reporter's reports of Unionist selections (1, 8 and 15 May 1958): Ballycassidy, Newporton, Drumderg, Lisbellaw, Castlecoole and Garvary; each was returned unopposed (Impartial Reporter, 22 May 1958, p. 7). Recorded for Nationalist-held divisions from the selection lists and first-meeting reports in the Fermanagh Herald: Holywell. Recorded from reports of the new council's meetings during the term: Newporton, Derrybrusk, Enniskillen Rural, Monea, Rahaltan, Coolyermor, Corrygloss, Killesher, Kinglass, Lisbofin, Florencecourt and Aghnaglack. Three members were co-opted at the first meeting (10 June 1958), all Unionists (one named Crawford); co-options are not election results. Ballyreagh's sitting member was deemed re-elected. Kinawley had no retiring member and was left vacant until the next election (S.R.&O. 1949 No. 18, reg. 15(1)). Tempo's retiring member, Mr. Arthur Fee, was deemed re-elected (no nomination). The earlier record carried 'Wm. McQuade' here from the 1955 return; the Impartial Reporter names 'William McQuaide'. Returned unopposed.
